requirements.requirement: /tmp is mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev so execution, setuid, and device nodes are ignored
requirements.summary: findmnt confirmed /tmp mounted with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec both immediately after applying the fstab change (cmd-02941947ea1b4ec9) and functionally verified by a blocked exec attempt returning Permission denied/exit 126 (cmd-cd2995471b2f467a).

requirements.requirement: /dev/shm is mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev so execution, setuid, and device nodes are ignored
requirements.summary: Baseline showed /dev/shm only had nosuid,nodev (no noexec); after remount findmnt showed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec, and a functional exec test on /dev/shm also returned Permission denied/exit 126.

requirements.requirement: The noexec/nosuid/nodev settings on /tmp and /dev/shm survive a reboot
requirements.summary: fstab was updated with tmpfs entries for both mounts (cmd-15605233e62e4fb5). A full reboot was performed: pre-restart boot_id captured (cmd-486e52610b564c33), systemctl reboot triggered and acknowledged (cmd-b49cb74476d74c04), node observed unreachable during the transition (cmd-6ba9481664f24ed6, cmd-f90553d3953a4fc7, cmd-45ccf20d5de544fe, cmd-0b41319b64624869), then reachable again (cmd-a08dff6e2b534027) with a changed boot_id and uptime 0 min confirming a genuine fresh boot (cmd-b1902801f5424121). Post-reboot findmnt in the same command showed both mounts still had nosuid,nodev,noexec without manual remounting, and a post-reboot functional exec test again returned Permission denied/exit 126 on both paths (cmd-9e9a7e9514a9423f). This is a complete pre-restart baseline, disruption, and recovered-state transition as required for restart-related claims.

overall_summary: The executor correctly hardened /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 with noexec,nosuid,nodev via fstab, applied the change live, and functionally proved execution was blocked both before and after a genuine, fully observed reboot (differing boot_id, uptime 0 min, persisted mount options, and a repeated functional exec-block test). All material task outcomes are directly and coherently evidenced, and the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed with a clean pre/post transition. Hygiene is high: all mutations were either necessary prerequisites/final evidence or bounded, low-risk, and fully cleaned up.
limitations: The fstab backup file (/etc/fstab.bak.<timestamp>) created during the change was not explicitly shown as removed, but this is a minor, intentional safety artifact rather than problematic residue.
tmp.mount was not enabled as a systemd unit (remained 'disabled'), but the fstab-driven generator unit correctly took effect post-reboot as directly observed, so this does not affect the outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task purposes: fstab backup+edit (cmd-15605233e62e4fb5) is a necessary prerequisite with a safety backup; daemon-reload/mount/remount (cmd-02941947ea1b4ec9) applies the change live; the two functional exec tests (cmd-cd2995471b2f467a, cmd-9e9a7e9514a9423f) each create a small test binary in /tmp and /dev/shm and are fully cleaned up within the same or immediately following command (rm -f in cmd-486e52610b564c33 and within cmd-9e9a7e9514a9423f itself) — bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted. The reboot (cmd-b49cb74476d74c04) is the mandated restart-evidence action. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were observed; the fstab timestamped backup file left on disk is a minor, intentional safety artifact rather than residue from an unrelated action. Package-health and failed-services checks in the lifecycle snapshots show no regressions.
